A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Wasserstein Flow Matching by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison despite substantial revision and reformatting.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original Gaussian-generation, shape-generation and genomics experiments, including WFM results in Tables 1–3 and additional evaluations in the appendices.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains original experiments and reports revised shape-generation results and biological evaluations in Tables 2–4, Figures 5–6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 2.3.1 corrects the BW tangent norm used by the stated Gaussian training loss: its mean term changes from ||a-m_mu||^2 to ||a||^2. This changes the written loss specification, without establishing an implementation change. The architectures, transport estimators, multisample coupling and generation procedures otherwise remain.

E1.justification: The spatial-transcriptomics evaluations are substantially reworked. Gaussian MERFISH microglial niches are replaced by seqFISH gut-tube niches, while point-cloud seqFISH organ niches are replaced by MERFISH Sst-neuron subtype niches. These change the evaluated populations and representations despite both assay names appearing previously. Other principal benchmark coverage remains.

E2.justification: Gaussian comparisons retain BW-FM with Euclidean updates and Frobenius FM. Both versions' Table 3 includes PointFlow, SoftFlow, DPF-Net, Shape-GF, PVD and PSF. The revised biological benchmarks do not introduce a different comparator set.

E3.justification: ShapeNet training and generation change from 1,000 to 2,048 points per shape. Point-cloud niche construction changes from 8 to 16 neighbors. The earlier default of 500,000 WFM training steps becomes 500,000 for ShapeNet and 100,000 for Table 4 experiments in v2 Appendix E.2. These are substantive reported protocol revisions, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds gene-expression case studies for Calb2+ and Th+ Sst-neuron niches in Figure 6, while removing v1's microglial composition-versus-cortical-depth analysis in Figure 3. The spiral sample-size comparison and shape interpolation/completion analyses remain, including material relocated to the appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new statistical approximation bounds in v2 are theoretical results, not uncertainty estimates for the reported experiments.

E6.justification: All six WFM ShapeNet scores change in Table 3; airplane CD/EMD changes from 73.45/71.72 to 69.88/64.44 under the revised point count. The Gaussian MERFISH row (1.90, 1.98, 2.06) is replaced by seqFISH (0.311, 0.531, 0.682). Point-cloud seqFISH scores of 61.79/64.34 are replaced by MERFISH scores of 52.80/54.52. Biological conditional accuracies and qualitative findings also change. These replacements do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit inner/outer regularity assumptions, Proposition 3.1, a conditional-flow derivation in Appendix B, and transport-map/geodesic approximation bounds in Appendix A.3. It also corrects Equation (4)'s interpolation parameter and the BW tangent norm. The new arguments contain internal inconsistencies, including Equation (21)'s factor of two relative to the stated logarithmic-map definition.

C1.justification: The abstract newly presents theoretical validation of conditional flows and the WFM objective as an explicit contribution; v1 emphasizes two algorithmic contributions. The principal claims about generating families of Gaussians and high-dimensional or variable-size point-clouds remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications concerning outer regularity, the gap between classical-OT theory and entropic implementation, and the informal general-Wasserstein derivation. Appendices A and E explain dimension-dependent estimation limits, the regularization accuracy–cost tradeoff, and quadratic scaling with point count. The transformer is identified as the main computational bottleneck, considerably qualifying the earlier scalability discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2 newly reports JAX/JIT execution, single-A100 hardware, approximately three days for ShapeNet training and three to four hours for Table 4 experiments. Appendix A changes from explicitly omitting an unregularized OT implementation to reporting CPU support in the codebase. Biological preprocessing documentation is also revised; the code destination remains equivalent.

R1.justification: A new single-cell generative-model discussion positions whole-population synthesis against cell-to-cell mappings, citing work by Gayoso, Cui, Theodoris, Klein and Eyring. The theoretical and scalability additions substantially expand engagement with OT literature. Existing comparisons with Riemannian, Fisher, Categorical and Meta Flow Matching remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the methods and experiments are rewritten around general distributions observed through point-cloud realizations. Background explanations are condensed, method subsections and appendices reorganized, and an Impact Statement added. The pervasive terminology and explanatory revisions extend beyond simply inserting new scientific content.

P2.justification: The main text changes to a two-column conference layout. v1 Figure 1 becomes separate Figure 1 and Table 1, and its spiral Figure 2 is split between the main text and appendix. Biological figures are replaced or added, the high-dimensional results table is transposed and grouped, and Table 3 gains colored ranking highlights.

improvement.justification: v2 improves documentation of assumptions, computational costs and limitations, adds biological diagnostics, and corrects earlier formulas. However, its advertised theoretical contribution has unresolved internal problems: Appendix A.3's claimed convergence rate does not follow from Equation (14) with the stated regularization choice, and Equation (21) contradicts the logarithmic-map definition. Changed populations and protocols also prevent interpreting lower scores as direct improvements. The documentation gains and uncertain reliability of the new theoretical support leave the overall quality change unresolved.
